text:
Brenden Dillon is 36, has 1,056 NHL games behind him from before this season, and is still the defenseman a coach reaches for when the lineup thins. He's been in and out of New Jersey's lineup, playing 12 of the team's games, but his last two were his biggest of the season: 18.5 and then 19.8 minutes in consecutive wins over Washington, the second on the night Devils rookie Silaev played his first NHL game. He picked up his first assist in the first of those.

He is what he has always been: a big body who hits (29 in 12 games), blocks shots and almost never shoots (three shots all year). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said as much about last season, his value isn't in creating offense.

The numbers around him are better than his line. The Devils have 57% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on the ice at five on five, and his results are running about four goals behind those chances. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last year. On a team that keeps winning, his role is depth and steadiness, and lately a lot more of both.
